releases.name: Context Churn Monitor v0.4.2: First public release
releases.body:
Agents can get stuck spending way too many tokens in context sinks, such as by repeatedly rereading the same files after every compactions. **Context Churn Monitor** shows how much context grew over a turn, alerts on repeated compactions, and gives you a step-by-step replay to see what happened exactly, with an optional automated LLM analysis to brainstorm what to fix in an instant.

This is the first GitHub release of Context Churn Monitor, and the first one considered stable, ready to be used in production (but consider this still in development). The plugin is safe to use anyway as it does not modify any of the user data, it's only an alerting system.

The repository and release archives already include the built plugin and panel.

## Get started

**OpenChamber 2.7.1 or newer:** Go to **Settings → Extensions → Add**, enter `https://github.com/lrq3000/context-churn-monitor`, and select **Import**. To install exactly this version, use the [v0.4.2 ZIP](https://github.com/lrq3000/context-churn-monitor/archive/refs/tags/v0.4.2.zip) instead. Approve the plugin and skills permissions to set up the backend and diagnostic skill for a local, managed OpenCode, and approve sidebar marks to see flagged sessions. Open **Context Churn Monitor** beside your chat, or as a workspace tab on mobile.

**OpenCode V2 without OpenChamber:** Extract the release ZIP to a stable directory and add its absolute path as the `package` in an OpenCode `plugins` entry. See the [OpenCode setup guide](https://github.com/lrq3000/context-churn-monitor/blob/v0.4.2/README.md#opencode-v2). This GitHub release does not update npm; at launch, the latest npm version is `0.4.1`.

## What you can do

- **Spot turns worth investigating.** Set separate thresholds for live context growth and compactions, or use rolling averages to catch a more gradual pattern. In OpenChamber, a sidebar mark takes you directly to the flagged session.
- **Replay what happened.** Open **View steps** to inspect model requests, tool calls and results, retries, and compactions in order. See where context grew between requests without mistaking that growth for a per-tool token count.
- **Choose what to share.** Export the captured evidence as standalone HTML or JSON. Monitoring, replay, and exports need no model calls. If you want model-assisted analysis, review the evidence preview before authorizing it.

**Fixed in 0.4.2:** OpenChamber sidebar scans now skip busy SQLite stores and retry on a later poll, so a locked store does not hold up the extension's startup health checks.

## What to know

- Context growth is measured relative to the model's window. A low reading can understate growth if the host exposes only part of the activity. A missing reading does not mean zero.
- The [Codex adapter](https://github.com/lrq3000/context-churn-monitor/blob/v0.4.2/README.md#codex) uses evidence from supported hooks. Fixtures and CLI input are tested; native Codex hook activation has not been verified.
- Replay and exports can contain prompts, commands, and tool output. Review them before sharing.
